results.name: core.schema.validate.valid
results.description: Validating a nested object that conforms. The happy path, paid on every tool call the framework makes.

results.name: core.schema.validate.invalid
results.description: Validating an object with four violations. Every violation is collected rather than short-circuiting, which is the point and also the cost.

results.name: core.schema.coerce
results.description: Repairing the near-miss arguments a model actually emits — a quoted number, a string boolean — before validation.

results.name: core.message.roundtrip
results.description: Serialising a multi-part message and reading it back. Every persisted session and every resumed workflow pays this per message.

results.name: core.ulid.generate
results.description: Generating a sortable identifier. Called at least once per event, and this framework publishes a lot of events.

results.name: core.events.publish.8listeners
results.description: Publishing one event to eight subscribers. The tax on observability being on by default.

results.name: core.retry.backoff
results.description: Computing a delay with decorrelated jitter. Cheap by design: a retry policy that costs real time is a retry policy that makes an outage worse.

results.name: core.context.child
results.description: Deriving a child context. Every agent step, tool call and workflow node creates one, so it sits on the hottest path there is.

results.name: tools.execute.trivial
results.description: Running a tool that returns immediately. Everything measured is framework overhead: lookup, coercion, validation, tracing, events.

results.name: tools.execute.rejected
results.description: A call whose arguments do not validate. The failure path is the one a model exercises repeatedly while it learns a schema, so it must not be the slow one.

results.name: tools.executeAll.8parallel
results.description: Eight read-only calls in one batch. Read-only calls run concurrently, so this measures the scheduling rather than the work.

results.name: llm.stream.assemble.500chunks
results.description: Assembling five hundred streamed deltas into one response, including reassembling fragmented tool-call JSON. Runs on the UI isolate while text is arriving, so it competes with frame budget.

results.name: llm.sse.decode.500events
results.description: Decoding five hundred server-sent events from a byte stream, including the chunk-boundary handling that makes it correct.

results.name: agents.turn.noTools
results.description: A whole agent turn against a model that answers instantly. The framework overhead of one step, with the provider taken out.

results.name: agents.turn.oneToolCall
results.description: A turn that calls one tool and then answers: two model calls, one tool execution, and the history bookkeeping between them.

results.name: agents.session.select.100messages
results.description: Choosing what history to send with a hundred messages already in the session. Runs before every model call, and grows with the conversation — which is exactly when a user is least patient.

results.name: memory.recall.5k
results.description: Rarity-weighted keyword recall over five thousand memories, blended with importance and recency. Runs on every turn of a remembering agent, so it is on the interactive path rather than the batch one.

results.name: vector.search.1k
results.description: Exhaustive search over 1k 768-dimensional vectors. The measurement behind the claim that brute force is fine on a device at this scale.

results.name: vector.search.10k
results.description: Exhaustive search over 10k 768-dimensional vectors. The measurement behind the claim that brute force is fine on a device at this scale.

results.name: vector.search.10k.filtered
results.description: Exhaustive search over 10k vectors with a metadata filter applied before ranking — the rule the port exists to enforce.

results.name: vector.upsert.1k
results.description: Writing a thousand 768-dimensional records. The ingestion side, which happens once where search happens constantly.

results.name: vector.cosine.768d
results.description: One cosine similarity. Multiplied by the index size on every unfiltered query, so it is the constant the whole scan is made of.

results.name: rag.chunk.recursive.100kb
results.description: Splitting a hundred kilobytes of prose at natural boundaries. Paid once per document at ingestion, and the reason ingestion is slow when it is slow.

results.name: rag.chunk.markdown.100kb
results.description: The same document split at headings, which also builds the heading path every chunk carries.

results.name: rag.bm25.build.5k
results.description: Building a BM25 index over five thousand chunks. The cost of the lexical half of hybrid retrieval, paid at start-up.

results.name: rag.bm25.search.5k
results.description: One BM25 query over five thousand chunks of varied prose. The claim this checks is that a keyword index is effectively free next to an embedding call.

results.name: rag.bm25.search.5k.commonTerms
results.description: The worst case, stated as one: every query term appears in every chunk, so the inverted index has no selectivity to offer and the query degrades to a full scan. Kept because a benchmark suite that only measures the happy path is a suite that flatters itself.

results.name: mcp.tool.call.roundtrip
results.description: One tool call across an MCP boundary, in process. Isolates the protocol cost — framing, correlation, translation — from the transport, which in a real deployment dominates it.
